brief: UBS reviews the October FOMC meeting: the Fed held the funds rate at 3.75%-4.00% but kept a tightening bias, upgrading growth language to a "strong pace" after upward 1H revisions and a 3% 3Q growth outlook. With labor resilient and inflation still elevated, UBS reads this as supporting further gradual tightening and retains its December and March hike calls. The 10-2 vote (Cook and Hammack dissenting hawkish) is read as a Committee prepared to hike in December, though Chair Warsh declined to confirm this and called the decision not predetermined. The press conference ran more dovish than the statement: Warsh cited improving inflation expectations despite firm data, flagged tighter financial and credit conditions since September, and said conditions are tighter but not yet "tight," implying the cycle is not over. He also pushed back on AI capex being necessarily inflationary. The Fed will cut 2027/2028 meeting counts to make room for strategy-only sessions; balance-sheet task force recommendations land near 1Q27 but UBS does not expect them to affect the current cycle. Front-end rates fell on the dovish tone; equities were muted. September core PCE, due the next day, is the key near-term catalyst.
